strings.name: Tu Youyou
strings.role: Pharmaceutical researcher · Pioneer of artemisinin research
strings.summary: Tu Youyou is a Chinese pharmaceutical researcher. Leading her research group in Project 523’s antimalarial work, she drew on traditional texts and drug screening to improve extraction from sweet wormwood, contributing to the discovery and validation of artemisinin. Subsequent research by several institutions jointly advanced drug development and clinical use. She received the Lasker–DeBakey Clinical Medical Research Award in 2011 and the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2015.
strings.coverageNote: Mainly covers artemisinin research and key honors through 2019. Emphasizes collaboration between institutions and does not provide live research updates.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Breakthrough in artemisinin research
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Improved low-temperature extraction and led a team in isolating the active ingredient and advancing tests of its antimalarial effects.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: International medical awards
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Received a Lasker Award in 2011 and a Nobel Prize in 2015 for the discovery of a new treatment for malaria.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Receives the Medal of the Republic
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Awarded the national Medal of the Republic for contributions including antimalarial drug research.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Receives the 2016 State Preeminent Science and Technology Award
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Shared the award for that year with Zhao Zhongxian; the award decision was announced in 2017.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Receives the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Recognized for discovering a new treatment against malaria, bringing global attention to artemisinin research.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Receives the Lasker clinical research award
strings.timeline.event-04.text: The award recognized her contributions to the discovery of artemisinin and the treatment of malaria.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Artemisinin receives a new drug certificate
strings.timeline.event-05.text: The research moved into drug approval and wider use, while development of subsequent derivatives continued.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Reports results to international colleagues
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Presented research on artemisinin and its derivatives at an antimalarial meeting supported by international organizations.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Studies dihydroartemisinin
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Obtained dihydroartemisinin during structural research, providing a basis for later artemisinin-based medicines.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Isolates artemisinin and advances clinical validation
strings.timeline.event-08.text: The team obtained the pure active ingredient and advanced early trials in patients.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Improves sweet wormwood extraction
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Inspired by ancient texts, adopted a low-temperature extraction approach that improved antimalarial activity and experimental consistency.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Leads her institute’s antimalarial research group
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Joined Project 523 research and organized the study of historical texts and screening of medicinal substances.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Graduates and joins a Chinese medicine research institute
strings.timeline.event-11.text: After completing pharmaceutical studies at Beijing Medical College, entered research into Chinese medicinal substances.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Born in Ningbo
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Born in Ningbo, Zhejiang, and later chose pharmaceutical science for her studies and research.
